title: Cyrus and the Crown
premise: Quentin Sterling keeps the ledgers of the Mnemosyne Guild, which buys, sells, and buries memories too dangerous to remember. When the border wards collapse and the stars go dark on the same night, she discovers her own stolen childhood holds the key to the wards' failure: she is the last heir of the dynasty that forged them. Hunted by a guild that wants its ledger balanced and a warlord who wants her bloodline extinguished, Quentin must choose between restoring the wards with a sacrifice that erases who she has become, or letting the long winter fall. In the end she forges a third path—rewriting the wards to run on freely given memory rather than royal blood—and pays for it with the guild's greatest treasure: her own name.
about_author: Gideon Ashgrove is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing other people's letters before turning to fiction about the things we refuse to remember. They write in a drafty house full of unlabeled boxes, insisting they know exactly what's in each one.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She audits the Mnemosyne Guild's vaults, trading in memories of first loves, crimes, and miracles, while hiding one vial she has never sold: her own childhood. Beat: competence masking a hollow core.

chapters.title: A Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The stars go out mid-audit; minutes later the border wards shatter like glass heard from miles away. The Guildmaster orders all ledgers sealed. Beat: dread arriving faster than understanding.

chapters.title: What the Vial Remembers
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Desperate clients flood the guild; among them a dying wardwright who recognizes Quentin's sealed vial and gasps a word—her true family name—before expiring. Beat: the past knocking loudly.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Balance
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Corvane's POV. He reveals he has always known what Quentin carries and offers a bargain: surrender the vial and her inheritance, and the guild will shield her from what's coming. Beat: betrayal wearing a mentor's face.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Unlit City
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She flees with the vial and one stolen ledger through streets gone lawless under starless dark, guided by a smuggler named Brannic who owes the guild a debt. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Memories Are Currency
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. He trades a happy memory to a fence for passage, showing Quentin how the poor survive by selling themselves piecemeal. Beat: empathy—the price of survival made intimate.

chapters.title: The Warlord's Herald
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A herald of the Ashen Warlord proclaims that the heir of the Ward-Kings lives and will be flayed for the old war. Quentin realizes her face is on every bounty board. Beat: identity becomes a death sentence.

chapters.title: The Archive Beneath the Ice
chapters.summary: Quentin and Brannic's POV, alternating. They reach a ruined archive where Quentin reads her ancestors' records: the wards were powered by royal memories, harvested generation after generation. Beat: horror at inheritance as consumption.

chapters.title: Corvane Closes the Book
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Corvane's POV. He dispatches retrievers, framing it as protecting the world from another ancient war—but privately he means to sell the vial to the highest bidder. Beat: institutional greed outpacing ideology.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Begins
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Frost creeps inland from the unwarded border; refugees speak of a cold that eats recollection itself. Quentin begins forgetting small things and fears the vial is leaking into her. Beat: erosion of self.

chapters.title: Brannic's Price
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. Cornered by retrievers, Brannic sells a memory of Quentin to buy their escape—betraying her without meaning to. Beat: guilt, and proof that everyone pays.

chapters.title: The Retrieval
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Captured by Corvane's retrievers, she talks her way into the guild's inner vault by offering something better than the vial: knowledge of where the Ward-Kings' original forge lies. Beat: wit as survival.

chapters.title: Inside the Vault of Herself
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Held in the guild, she finally opens her own vial and relives her childhood: her mother sealing the wards, her bloodline's complicity, why her memory was taken. Beat: grief and terrible clarity.

chapters.title: An Ancient War, Remembered
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Flashback chapters from the vial reveal the first war was fought over who would be consumed to power the wards—and the Ashen Warlord's people were the fuel. Beat: the enemy's grievance becomes understandable.

chapters.title: Two Fires
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The Warlord's envoy offers Quentin an alliance: let the winter fall, end the wards forever, and no bloodline will ever be harvested again. Beat: temptation of a just cause built on ruin.

chapters.title: The Forge of Kings
chapters.summary: Quentin, Brannic, and a defecting retriever's POV. They race to the forge ahead of both armies, Brannic confessing his betrayal en route. Beat: forgiveness earned at knife-point.

chapters.title: Corvane's Ledger Balanced
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Corvane's POV. At the forge, Corvane attempts to bind Quentin to the wards himself—a final harvest. His own sold memories turn on him; the ledger collects its debt. Beat: poetic downfall.

chapters.title: The Choice of the Last Heir
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Alone at the anvil, she faces the binary: restore the old wards with her bloodline's memories, or let the winter win. She chooses neither. Beat: defiance of the story written for her.

chapters.title: A New Covenant
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She reforges the wards to accept freely given memory, offering her own first—and the refugees, smugglers, and even former retrievers begin adding theirs. Beat: collective sacrifice replacing inherited suffering.

chapters.title: The Stars Return
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The wards ignite; stars reappear over a battered but unbroken land. The Warlord's army halts at a border that now belongs to everyone who fed it. Beat: hard-won dawn.

chapters.title: The Woman With No Name
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. Quentin, having paid her name into the wards, walks unrecognized through the city she saved. Brannic finds her anyway—he kept one memory back, deliberately. Beat: identity beyond lineage.

chapters.title: Cyrus and the Crown
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Opening a new ledger, she writes the first entry under a chosen name—Cyrus—and closes the guild's era of impossible trade. Some things should not be for sale. Beat: quiet, earned beginning.
